avoid_supplements.name: Methotrexate
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Both agents inhibit dihydrofolate reductase and compete for renal secretion, significantly increasing methotrexate toxicity and bone marrow suppression risk
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid concurrent use; if essential, monitor CBC, renal function, and methotrexate levels closely

avoid_supplements.name: High-dose Folic Acid (>5mg daily)
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Excessive folic acid may reduce sulfamethoxazole efficacy by competing with PABA metabolism and antagonizing the drug's mechanism
avoid_supplements.action: Limit folic acid supplementation to ≤1mg daily; use only if prescribed for folate deficiency prevention

avoid_supplements.name: Warfarin
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Sulfamethoxazole inhibits CYP2C9 and displaces warfarin from protein binding, increasing anticoagulant effect and bleeding risk
avoid_supplements.action: Monitor INR frequently; adjust warfarin dose as needed; consider alternative antibiotic if possible

caution_supplements.name: Para-Aminobenzoic Acid (PABA)
caution_supplements.mechanism: PABA is a competitive substrate for the same folate synthesis pathway that sulfamethoxazole inhibits, potentially reducing antibiotic efficacy
caution_supplements.action: Monitor clinical response; avoid high-dose PABA supplements during treatment

caution_supplements.name: Phenytoin
caution_supplements.mechanism: Both agents induce and compete for CYP2C9 metabolism; sulfamethoxazole may increase phenytoin levels
caution_supplements.action: Monitor phenytoin levels and seizure control; adjust dosing if necessary

caution_foods.name: High-dose vitamin supplements containing folate analogs
caution_foods.mechanism: Excessive dietary folate supplementation may reduce sulfamethoxazole antimicrobial efficacy
caution_foods.action: Maintain normal dietary folate intake; avoid megavitamin formulations during antibiotic therapy

monitoring_notes: Monitor for crystalluria, hematologic toxicity (CBC), and hepatorenal function throughout therapy. Educate patients to maintain adequate hydration to minimize kidney stone risk and to report signs of Stevens-Johnson syndrome or severe hypersensitivity reactions immediately.
